newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel ex-boss, managers, in sleaze trial.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel ex-boss, managers, in sleaze trial.

text.p: The former chairman of French industrial group Alcatel Alsthom and about 40 other managers went on trial on Tuesday accused of plundering company funds to pay for work on their private homes.

Pierre Suard -- forced to resign as head of France's biggest industrial firm in June 1995 -- plus a dozen other former Alcatel managers and about 30 bosses of other companies are charged with abuse of corporate funds.
Investigating magistrate Jean-Marie d'Huy launched the probe in March 1993, ordering the detention of two sacked employees of telecommunications equipment unit Alcatel CIT.
The two, Jose Corral and Antoine Leal, were allegedly involved in an overcharging scam. The subsidiary's chairman Pierre Guichet was placed under investigation in 1994, and Suard in July that year.
According to investigators, Suard had his company pay for work at three of his private residences including five million francs ($900,000) on security systems at one of his homes.

Suard said shortly after he was placed under investigation that the work at his homes in Boulogne-Billancourt and Neuilly-sur-Seine outside Paris were "professional expenses taken care of by the group".
He said that they followed the murder of Renault president Georges Besse by urban guerrillas Action Directe in late 1986.
But critics said it was unacceptable that a corporate executive earning 1.2 million francs a month should charge the company for work which news magazines reported included fitting a kitchen.

The probe also led D'Huy to explore widespread alleged overbilling of key client France Telecom, in an investigation which has not yet been completed. Guichet was released from prison in December 1994 but remains barred from doing his job.

Suard was forced to step down because D'Huy had placed him under strict judicial controls which barred him from running the company or talking to colleagues. He resigned in June 1995 and was replaced by former Total SA chairman Serge Tchuruk.
